pr_title: Add missing on error manifest struct destroy in pluginscript script init

issue_context.title: Pluginscript script init skip manifest destroy on error
issue_context.body:
In pluginscript initializing a script is done by calling a callback which should return a `godot_pluginscript_script_manifest` structure.
Given this structure contains dictionary and array, it should be destroyed once no longer used:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/6f38aeef5255d1fdeb99d727a0f67b9be6ccdf36/modules/gdnative/pluginscript/pluginscript_script.cpp#L320-L326

However this is currently not the case if the callback returns an error:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/6f38aeef5255d1fdeb99d727a0f67b9be6ccdf36/modules/gdnative/pluginscript/pluginscript_script.cpp#L254-L257

I would say forcing the callback to always return a valid manifest seems a cleaner approach (especially considering with the right flags, a C compiler would warn agains returning an initialized variable).

However this change in behaviour may break compatibily (returning an uninitialized manifest cause a segfault).

On top of that this leak is obviously not that of a really big deal because 1) we only leak at most one manifest (so 2 strings, 3 arrays and 1 dictionary) per script whose initialization failed and 2) script initialization failure means user code is obviously buggy (so this should not happened in production)

However it seems [very very few project would be affected](https://github.com/search?q=godot_pluginscript_script_manifest+-extension%3Ah+-filename%3Ascript.py+-filename%3Apluginscript.cpp&type=Code)

In fact only godot-python and godot-ruby would be really affected (godot-clisp is an early WIP).
Given I maintain godot-python, we end up with only godot-ruby, so I guess the change is acceptable ;-)

review_comments: Please also `#undef FREE_SCRIPT_MANIFEST` after the last use.
